statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail remains in the low band while bond, oil and geopolitical Stress remains extreme.
recommendation: Current conditions are assessed as low Tail with extreme Stress; the main conditional checkpoint is the U.S. cash-open and state-employment release window.
headline: European-morning stabilization keeps Tail low while yields, oil and Hormuz disruption sustain extreme Stress
body: Nasdaq futures are modestly firmer, but U.S. Treasury yields have resumed rising and Brent remains above $93 after touching a one-month high. European equities are little changed and no persistent one-way NQ continuation is independently verified. Strait of Hormuz traffic remains severely constrained.

lookbackSummary: Across the prior 24 clock hours, Tail rose from low morning readings into WATCH/BLOCK during Thursday's U.S. selloff, peaked at 29% late in the session, then decayed overnight as futures stabilized.
outlookSummary: Risk is concentrated around 15:25–16:30 Berlin for U.S. cash-open price discovery and the state-employment release. Conditional Tail peaks at 24% and remains below the block threshold unless persistent one-way structure with weak retracements is observed; Friday's futures close then shifts risk toward weekend headline and reopening-gap uncertainty.

forecast.analysis: Observed European-morning conditions are mixed: Nasdaq futures are modestly firmer, while Treasury yields have resumed rising and Brent remains above $93. No persistent one-way NQ structure is independently verified.

forecast.analysis: European morning trading is a retracement-quality checkpoint. Tail stays low if the overnight stabilization persists despite higher yields and oil; renewed directional extension would challenge that assumption.
Late European morning shifts attention toward U.S. premarket liquidity. Balanced index trade would keep Tail low, while synchronized megacap weakness and rising yields would raise conditional risk.
U.S. premarket participation becomes more informative. Tail remains low unless price begins holding near downside extremes with shallow rebounds and broader cross-asset confirmation.
Approaching the U.S. opening sequence lifts conditional Tail into WATCH. The market direction is still unobserved; the key issue is whether pre-open structure becomes persistently one-way.

The U.S. cash open is imminent. Conditional Tail is higher because Thursday ended weak and yields remain elevated, but a block still requires observed opening continuation with poor retracement quality.

First-hour cash price discovery overlaps the 16:00 Berlin state labor release. Tail peaks at 24%; only observed persistent extension with shallow or failed retracements would justify crossing the block threshold.

Post-release price discovery remains WATCH conditionally. Tail would fall if the opening move retraces meaningfully and breadth stabilizes; repeated extension after failed rebounds would keep risk elevated.
Late-morning U.S. trade tests whether the opening move can sustain itself. Improving breadth and deeper pullbacks would support further Tail decay; renewed extension would delay normalization.
Midday liquidity usually favors more two-sided trade. Tail returns to low conditionally if the morning move has not developed persistent directional efficiency.
Early afternoon remains a structure check rather than an event window. Stable yields and meaningful intraday retracements would keep Tail low.
Afternoon trade stays low-Tail conditionally if cross-asset pressure does not re-align. Renewed megacap and semiconductor weakness with rising yields would be the main invalidation.
The U.S. power hour raises conditional continuation risk before the Friday close. Tail remains WATCH unless a late directional move begins extending with weak pullbacks.
Cash-market closing price discovery can remain noisy. Tail is WATCH only conditionally; orderly closing auctions and stable cross-assets would favor a quick decline in risk.
The futures market approaches its Friday close. With live price discovery ending, Tail reflects residual headline and gap risk rather than an observed persistent path.
Weekend closure removes live NQ path evidence. Stress remains extreme because oil, bond-market fragility and Gulf shipping risks can affect the next reopening gap.
With NQ closed, no directional price-path claim is made. Tail stays low while geopolitical and rates-related headline risk remains elevated for the eventual reopening.
Saturday overnight remains a closed-market interval. Tail is low because no path is observable; Stress stays extreme due to unresolved energy and sovereign-yield risks.
No live futures structure is available during the weekend closure. Risk is therefore concentrated in potential headline-driven reopening gaps rather than current directional efficiency.
The closed-market interval continues. Tail remains low absent observed price structure, while persistent Gulf and bond-market risks keep Stress elevated.
Weekend conditions remain unobservable in NQ. A later reassessment should depend on actual reopening behavior rather than assuming that current headlines create a one-way move.
The market remains closed, so Tail stays low and conditional. Energy supply disruption and elevated sovereign yields remain the principal background Stress drivers.
No live Nasdaq futures path is available. Tail remains low while confidence is slightly reduced because weekend headlines cannot yet be translated into observed price behavior.
The 24-hour horizon ends during the weekend closure. Tail remains low without observed one-way structure; geopolitical and rates risks remain important for the next reopening assessment.
